items.text: US stocks rose sharply in a holiday-shortened session that closed at 1 p.m. ET. The Dow gained 1.18% to 50,774.94, the S&P 500 1.60% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq 2.31% to 24,129.50. Chip stocks led a rebound in technology shares, with the PHLX Semiconductor index up 4.69%. For the week the S&P 500 rose about 5.6% and the Nasdaq about 6.7%. Newly listed Anthropic jumped about 11% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price after a volatile first week. Brent crude traded near $97 after attacks on Saudi energy sites and tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and futures markets still lean towards a Fed rate rise in December.
items.notes: Closing figures match across JBizNews and Motley Fool. Some secondary sources (mlq.ai) describe it as the S&P's best week since April 2025; I couldn't open them. Oil figures come from The National (thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/11/27/oil-set-to-post-weekly-gain...): Brent was $97.49 mid-morning UAE time and on track for a ~7% weekly gain. Anthropic is also relevant to the 'Anthropic IPO and AI market valuations' thread. The WaPo/AP index wrap was blocked.

items.text: US shoppers spent a record $7.1 billion online on Thanksgiving Day, up 10.4% from a year earlier and above Adobe's $6.9 billion forecast, according to Adobe Analytics figures released on Friday. Adobe expects $12.9 billion in online spending on Black Friday (up 9.2%), $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday and $47.5 billion across Cyber Week. Season-to-date online spending from Nov 1 to 22 topped $82.5 billion, up 9.1%. Mobile devices made up 63.2% of Thanksgiving spending, and Adobe said AI-driven traffic to retail sites rose 162%. Final Black Friday figures were not out at the time of writing.
items.outlet: Pirates & Princesses (citing Adobe Analytics, Seeking Alpha, TipRanks)
items.notes: Link1 is a weak outlet that compiles Adobe data. Link2 (Seeking Alpha) and a Reuters item on US News ('US Black Friday online sales to cross $13 billion, Adobe says', 2026-11-27) appeared in search but I couldn't open them; the Reuters headline rounds to 'over $13bn'. Swap in a Reuters/AP link if one is available. Adobe's numbers are nominal, not inflation-adjusted.

items.text: Hackers breached Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship cloud platform, Reuters reported in an exclusive citing unnamed sources. Cloud One runs on Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle infrastructure and hosts payroll, maintenance logistics, a munitions-tracking system used at more than 200 sites, and a command-and-control system that processes North American air-defence radar feeds. Sources said the intrusion was found during an upgrade in the past several weeks and that the attackers reached the platform's control layer. In response the Air Force reportedly paused migrations, blocked updates and revoked some administrator rights. Cyber Command is assessing the damage. The Air Force declined to comment on specific systems. It is unknown who the attackers were or whether data was taken.
items.notes: The original is a Reuters exclusive (usnews.com/news/top-news/articles/2026-11-27/exclusive-hackers-breach-us-air-force-flagship-cloud-one-computing-platform); I couldn't open it. Reports differ on how many anonymous sources Reuters had: Military.com says five, Forbes says three. The Daily Beast framed it as a blow to Hegseth. Military.com says it could not independently confirm the report. No official confirmation.

items.text: Trump wrote on Truth Social that the US backs Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's efforts to stop oil smuggling, end corruption and bring all weapons under exclusive state control, and that Washington wants a united Iraq that makes its own political decisions. The post came as Baghdad moved to take federal control of Kurdistan Region border crossings and oilfields. Iraq's top court ruled that federal forces can deploy on all borders, which prompted protests in the Kurdish region. Al-Zaidi recently also ordered troops against the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah at Jurf al-Sakhar. Analysts quoted by AFP say the drive fits the US maximum-pressure policy on Iran. A Baghdad dialogue meeting is set for Dec 1.
items.outlet: Al Jazeera (with AFP, Reuters); The National
items.notes: The Truth Social post is primary and both outlets quote it the same way. Al Jazeera stresses the Kurdish protests and the risk of antagonising Iran. The National notes Trump claimed credit for al-Zaidi's premiership and says US troops left Iraq in late September.

items.text: Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving, Trump defended his friendship with Vladimir Putin, saying the goal is to stop the killing and that the main obstacle to peace is that Putin and Zelensky really hate each other. He said he did not know whether Putin would attend the G20 summit in Miami on Dec 14–15, but that Putin certainly can come if he wants. He also played down reports of Russian and Chinese intelligence help to Iran, saying China is very little involved and Russia gives little. In a BBC interview Zelensky called the Trump–Putin friendship strange and said Putin cannot be a friend.
items.notes: E-261127-57 already logged the Truth Social 'pull back' post. What's new here is the remark that Putin can come to the G20 and the comments on Iran's backers. The Iran remarks come from the Times of Israel live blog (timesofisrael.com/liveblog-november-27-2026/), which doesn't timestamp them. The Kremlin says no decision on G20 attendance.

items.text: State measles counts kept rising over the holiday week. Minnesota reported 228 cases this year, its most since 1990, with 25 new in the past week, mostly children in Todd County. Wisconsin has at least 918 confirmed cases since August, including at least 88 in the past week, 19 hospitalisations and three deaths this month (two children and an adult in Lafayette County). Officials say 99% of cases were unvaccinated or of unknown status. Ohio has 400 cases in 30 counties, against 45 in all of 2025. The CDC's national count stood at 6,038 cases as of Nov 25.
items.reporter: MPR News Staff; Chad Murphy, James Powel, Mary Walrath-Holdridge (USA TODAY Network)
items.outlet: MPR News; Columbus Dispatch via Yahoo
items.notes: The figures come from state health departments. The national death count is still disputed: the CDC says 9, Reuters' tally of state figures says 14 (see E-261126-09).

items.text: The EPA said its first post-detonation lab results found no lead in 38 public drinking-water samples taken after the Army blew up about five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Nov 25. Its real-time air monitors recorded no detectable airborne lead for 30 hours afterwards. Low lead levels found before the blast at four sites in Illinois and Missouri, all well under the 15 ppb action level, were put down to existing conditions. The EPA has taken more than 3,200 air, water, soil and dust samples and says tap-water, soil and dust results will follow over the coming days.
items.notes: Newsweek covers the air results (from Thursday's EPA update). The 38-sample water result comes only from GSM Global, a low-profile aggregator citing an EPA release of Nov 27. Check against the EPA response page if possible.

items.text: Travel and power were recovering after the Thanksgiving coastal storm. Outages that peaked above 900,000 customers on Thursday evening had roughly halved by Friday afternoon, but several hundred thousand customers from Missouri and Illinois to New Jersey and New York were still without power. More than 1,200 US flights were cancelled on Thanksgiving Day and thousands delayed. Disruption eased on Friday, though delays continued at Boston Logan and New York-area airports. Parts of eastern Missouri got up to 15 inches of snow. Transportation Secretary Duffy had earlier blamed most holiday delays on weather. The FAA expects about 417,000 flights over Nov 23–Dec 1, with the return rush still to come.
items.notes: Both links are from the same lesser-known outlet. I couldn't open any wire or FlightAware/poweroutage.us confirmation. No deaths reported in this source. Domain set to Infrastructure because E-261127-06 already covers the storm itself.

items.text: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was moved from Thursday to Saturday, Nov 28, at 8:30 a.m. because of the coastal storm. Macy's announced the change on Nov 25, and CBS New York says it is the first weather postponement in the parade's history; the only earlier break was the 1942–44 wartime suspension, when helium was needed for the war. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani had warned of gusts up to 65 mph, and Gov. Hochul declared a state of emergency for New York City and nearby counties. Some out-of-town marching bands had trouble staying for the new date.
items.reporter: Jesse Zanger, Marcia Kramer (CBS New York)
items.notes: The decision came on Nov 25 but wasn't in recent_events. The parade takes place after this brief is written. The marching-band detail comes from a CNN headline of Nov 27 that I couldn't open.

items.text: Chief Judge Stephanie Rose of the federal court for the Southern District of Iowa ordered ICE to release Guatemalan immigrant Santos Fredy Perez Recinos from the Polk County Jail within 24 hours. Officers looking for a different man wanted on a state sexual-assault warrant arrested Perez Recinos on Oct 28. After they realised the mistake, the ICE office in Des Moines told them to keep holding him on an immigration warrant. Rose found that re-detaining him without a bond hearing, years after he was released as an unaccompanied minor and with no change in circumstances, violated due process. She called the error almost beyond belief and said such mistakes appear to be increasing.
items.notes: Both links are the same Iowa Capital Dispatch story; the original wouldn't load and KCRG did. The exact ruling date isn't given, only that it came days before Nov 27. Like E-261127-08 (Sabraw), it's part of a pattern of judges limiting re-detention of released immigrants without changed circumstances. Separately and from one source only: Wisevoter, citing Alabama Political Reporter, says the US Attorney in Mobile is appealing Judge Beaverstock's order limiting warrantless construction-site raids to the 11th Circuit (Nov 27). Not logged.

items.text: Andrea Stewart-Cousins, majority leader of the New York State Senate, died on Friday aged 76, her office said, without giving a cause. A senator since 2006, she became leader in 2019, the first woman and first Black woman to lead the chamber. She also chaired the board of the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee, Democrats' national arm for state legislative races. She was re-elected on Nov 3 and kept as leader by her conference in mid-November. Gov. Kathy Hochul ordered flags on state buildings flown at half-staff. Succession details are expected in the coming weeks.
items.outlet: AP (via Northern Virginia Daily); WRGB CBS 6 Albany
items.notes: This is state-level news, included because it was national wire copy and her DLCC role is national. Drop if space is tight.

items.text: The comment period on CMS's proposed exchange pre-eligibility verification rule (Working Families Tax Cut Act implementation) closed on Nov 26. The proposal would require verification of eligibility before subsidised marketplace enrolment, starting with 2028 coverage. No final rule or comment tally has been published.
items.notes: Rule R-261026-02 moved from Open for comment to Proposed (comment closed).
